en: Habban ibn Musa narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak reported to us: Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli reported to us; (and a different chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanthali, Muhammad ibn Rafi', and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—Ibn Rafi' said: narrated to us, while the other two said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq reported to us: Ma'mar reported to us—and the wording is the hadith of Ma'mar from the narration of 'Abd and Ibn Rafi'. Yunus and Ma'mar both said, from az-Zuhri: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Urwah ibn az-Zubayr, 'Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud informed me about the narration of 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, when the people of the slander said concerning her what they said, and Allah declared her innocent of what they said. Each of them narrated to me a portion of her narration, and some of them retained more of her hadith than others and were more precise in recounting it. I retained from each one of them the hadith he narrated to me, and parts of their accounts confirm one another. They mentioned that 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, intended to set out on a journey, he would cast lots among his wives, and whichever of them had her lot drawn, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would take her out with him. 'A'ishah said: So he cast lots among us during a military expedition that he undertook, and my lot was drawn, so I set out with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and that was after the veil (hijab) had been revealed. I was carried in my howdah and set down in it throughout our travel. When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished his expedition and returned, and we drew near to Madinah, he announced the departure by night. I stood up when they announced the departure and walked until I went past the army. When I had relieved myself, I headed back toward my conveyance. I touched my chest and discovered that my necklace of Zafar onyx had broken off and fallen. So I returned and searched for my necklace, and searching for it detained me. Meanwhile, the group of men who used to saddle the camel for me came, lifted my howdah, and strapped it onto my camel which I had been riding, assuming that I was inside it. She said: Women in those days were light; they had not become heavy or covered in flesh, as they only ate morsels of food. Thus the men did not think anything of the lightness of the howdah when they lifted and raised it, and I was a young woman of tender age. So they drove the camel forward and departed. I found my necklace after the army had moved on, and when I arrived at their camp, there was no one calling and no one answering. So I made my way to the spot where I had been staying, thinking that the people would miss me and return for me. While I was sitting in my place, my eyes overcame me and I fell asleep. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal as-Sulami, then adh-Dhakwani, had lagged behind the army to rest, and he set out late in the night and reached my place by morning. He saw the dark outline of a person sleeping, so he came to me and recognized me when he saw me, as he had seen me before the veil had been enjoined upon me. I awoke at his saying: "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un (Indeed to Allah we belong, and to Him we shall return)," when he recognized me, so I immediately veiled my face with my outer garment (jilbab). By Allah, he did not speak a single word to me, nor did I hear any word from him other than his reciting: "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un," until he made his camel kneel down and stepped on its front knee, so I mounted it. He set out leading the camel with me until we reached the army after they had halted to rest in the intense heat of midday. There perished on account of me those who perished, and the one who took upon himself the greater share of it was 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. We arrived in Madinah, and I fell ill for a whole month upon our arrival in Madinah, while the people were indulging in the gossip of the people of the slander, and I was completely unaware of any of that. But what caused me doubt during my illness was that I did not perceive from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the tenderness that I used to see from him whenever I fell ill; the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would merely enter, greet, and then say: "How is that one of yours?" That caused me doubt, but I sensed no evil until I went out after having begun to recover. Umm Mistah went out with me toward al-Manasi', which was our open place of relieving ourselves, and we would not go out except from night to night. That was before we built privies near our houses, and our custom was like the custom of the early Arabs regarding open spaces, as we were troubled by privies being built near our homes. So Umm Mistah and I went out—she was the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn 'Amir, maternal aunt of Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, and her son was Mistah ibn Uthathah ibn 'Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. The daughter of Abu Ruhm and I returned toward my house when we had finished our affair. Umm Mistah tripped over her woollen cloak and exclaimed: "May Mistah perish!" I said to her: "How wretched is what you have said! Do you curse a man who attended Badr?" She said: "O you there! Have you not heard what he said?" I asked: "And what did he say?" She said: So she informed me of what the people of the slander had said, and that added illness to my illness. When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, entered upon me, greeted, and then said: "How is that one of yours?" I said: "Do you permit me to go to my parents?" She said: At that time, I wanted to verify the news through them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gave me permission, so I came to my parents and said to my mother: "O my mother, what are the people talking about?" She said: "O my little daughter, take it easy on yourself, for by Allah, rarely has there been a beautiful woman with a husband who loves her, having co-wives, except that they say much against her." She said: I said: "Subhanallah! Have people really been talking about this?" She said: So I wept that entire night until morning came, my tears never ceasing and my eyes finding no sleep; then I awoke weeping. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd when the revelation was delayed, to consult them about separating from his wife. She said: As for Usamah ibn Zayd, he advised the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and according to the affection he held in his heart for them, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing of them except good." As for 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, he said: "Allah has not constrained you, and women besides her are plenty; if you ask the slave-girl, she will tell you the truth." She said: So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called Bariirah and said: "O Bariirah, have you seen anything that causes you doubt regarding 'A'ishah?" Bariirah said to him: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, if I have ever seen anything in her to fault her for, it is nothing more than that she is a young girl of tender age who sleeps and neglects her family's dough, so the household sheep comes and eats it." She said: Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood upon the pulpit and sought someone to vindicate him against 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. She said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said while upon the pulpit: "O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me against a man whose harm has reached my household? For by Allah, I have known nothing of my family except good, and they have mentioned a man of whom I have known nothing except good, and he never entered upon my family except with me." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari stood up and said: "I will excuse you against him, O Messenger of Allah! If he is from al-Aws, we will strike his neck, and if he is from our brothers of al-Khazraj, give us your order and we will carry out your command." She said: Then Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah stood up—he was the leader of al-Khazraj, and he was a righteous man, but tribal zealotry overtook him—and said to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: "You have lied, by the life of Allah! You will not kill him, nor are you able to kill him." Then Usayd ibn Hudayr stood up—he was the cousin of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh—and said to Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah: "You have lied, by the life of Allah! We will certainly kill him, for you are a hypocrite arguing on behalf of hypocrites!" The two tribes, al-Aws and al-Khazraj, became agitated until they were about to fight one another, while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, continued calming them until they became quiet, and he fell silent. She said: I wept that whole day, my tears never ceasing and my eyes finding no sleep; then I wept through the following night, my tears never ceasing and my eyes finding no sleep, while my parents thought that my weeping would burst my liver. While they were both sitting with me and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter upon me, so I gave her permission, and she sat down weeping. She said: While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, entered upon us, greeted, and sat down. She said: He had not sat with me since what was said had been said, and a month had passed without any revelation coming to him regarding my affair. She said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, recited the Tashahhud when he sat down, then said: "To proceed: O 'A'ishah, it has reached me concerning you such-and-such. If you are innocent, Allah will soon declare your innocence; and if you have committed a sin, then ask Allah for forgiveness and repent to Him, for when the servant admits a sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance." She said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, finished his speech, my tears dried up completely until I did not feel a single drop of them. I said to my father: "Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf regarding what he said." He said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him." Then I said to my mother: "Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf." She said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him." So I said, while I was a young girl of tender age who did not recite much of the Quran: "By Allah, I know that you have heard this until it has settled in your souls and you have believed it. So if I tell you that I am innocent—and Allah knows that I am innocent—you will not believe me; and if I admit to you something—and Allah knows that I am innocent—you will believe me. By Allah, I find no example for myself and you except as the father of Yusuf said: {'Patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One sought for help against that which you describe'}." She said: Then I turned away and lay down on my bed. She said: And by Allah, I knew at that time that I was innocent and that Allah would exonerate me by virtue of my innocence, but by Allah, I never thought that revelation to be recited would be revealed regarding my affair; my status in my own eyes was too insignificant for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to speak concerning me with a matter that would be recited. But I used to hope that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would see a dream in his sleep through which Allah would declare my innocence. She said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had not moved from where he was sitting, nor had anyone of the household gone out, before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down revelation upon His Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He was overcome by the severe hardship that used to overtake him during revelation, to the extent that drops of sweat like pearls would roll down from him on a freezing winter day, because of the weight of the Speech that was being revealed to him. She said: When that state was lifted from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he was smiling, and the first word he spoke was that he said: "Rejoice, O 'A'ishah! As for Allah, He has declared your innocence." My mother said to me: "Stand up and go to him." I said: "By Allah, I will not stand up to go to him, and I will praise none other than Allah; He is the One Who revealed my innocence." She said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {"Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you..."} ten verses. Thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses declaring my innocence. She said: Abu Bakr—who used to spend on Mistah because of his kinship to him and his poverty—said: "By Allah, I will never spend anything on him ever again after what he said about 'A'ishah!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {"And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give aid to their relatives..."} up to His words: {"Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?"}. Habban ibn Musa said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: "This is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah." Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, I certainly love that Allah should forgive me!" So he restored to Mistah the expenditure that he used to provide for him, and said: "I will never withhold it from him, ever." 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had also asked Zaynab bint Jahsh, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, about my affair: "What do you know or what have you seen?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, I guard my hearing and my sight; by Allah, I know nothing but good." 'A'ishah said: And she was the one among the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who rivaled me, but Allah protected her through piety; while her sister Hamnah bint Jahsh began fighting on her behalf, so she perished among those who perished. Az-Zuhri said: This is what has reached us concerning the affair of those people. And he said in the hadith of Yunus: "zealotry overcame him."
